[[File:My good fortune in Auschwitz.webm|upright=1.35|thumb|Short movie ''My good fortune in Auschwitz''. Mostly about his friendship with fellow prisoner Jos Slagter (1907–1977)]]
'''Hajo Meyer''' ({{IPA|de|ˈhaːjo ˈmaɪɐ}}; {{langx|he|האיו מאייר}}; born '''Hans-Joachim Gustav Meyer''', {{IPA|de|hans ˈjoːaxɪm ˈɡʊstaf ˈmaɪɐ|pron}}; 12 August 1924 – 23 August 2014) was a German-born Dutch [[physicist]], [[Holocaust survivor]] and [[political activism|political activist]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Verhey|first=Elma|title=Interview – Hajo Meyer|date=September 2006 |publisher=Tribune, [[Socialist Party (Netherlands)]]|url=http://www.sp.nl/nieuws/tribune/200609/interview_hajo_meyer.shtml|accessdate=2 May 2010}}</ref> While primarily known for his public commentaries in terms of the [[European Jewish]] community, he is also noted for his work directing the facility [[Philips Natuurkundig Laboratorium]] for many years. In this capacity Meyer played a role in developing the [[ASML]] wafer stepper, a photolithography machine used in the production of integrated circuits (ICs) on silicon wafers.<ref>{{cite book |last=Raaijmakers |first=René |date=2019 |title=ASML's Architects: The Story of the Engineers who Shaped the World's Most Powerful Chip Machines |location=Nijmegen |publisher=Techwatch Books |isbn=978-9082707427 |chapter=Chapter 5: The violin maker}}</ref>

==Early life==
Meyer was born on 12 August 1924, as the youngest of three brothers, in [[Bielefeld]], Germany, to Therese ({{nee}} Melchior) and Gustav Meyer, a [[notary]] who had fought in the [[First World War]].<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://archive.org/details/feminismsocialis00meye | url-access=registration | quote=To the memory of my parents Gustav. |title = The Feminism and socialism of Lily Braun| publisher=INDIANA University Press |isbn = 9780253321695|last1 = Meyer|first1 = Alfred G.|year = 1985}}</ref><ref name=smolinski>[https://smolinski.nl/wp/blog/2023/03/20/hajo-meyer/ Hajo Meyer], Smolinski Foundation, 20 March 2023, retrieved 25 June 2025</ref> Meyer was [[Jewish]].<ref>[https://www.jpost.com/diaspora/antisemitism/german-court-oks-labeling-anti-zionist-activist-as-antisemite-538241 By Benjamin Weinthal, January 19, 2018, The Jerusalem Post], A Frankfurt court ruled in 2007 that Melzer and the late anti-Zionist Jew Hajo Meyer can be called "experts on applied Judeophobia".</ref> At age 14, he was sent by his parents from [[Nazi Germany]] to the Netherlands on 4 January 1939 as part of a [[Kindertransport]] convoy, and settled in Holland on his own. Their decision was made after Hajo was no longer permitted to attend school in the aftermath of [[Kristallnacht]]. His parents' maxim was: 'We do not dote to death on children' (''bei uns gibt es keine {{ill|Affenliebe|de}}'').<ref name="Briefe" >Hajo G. Meyer, [https://books.google.com/books?id=UuYOBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA9  ''Briefe eines Flüchtlings 1939–1945: Ein jüdischer Junge im holländischen Exil,'']  Frank & Timme GmbH, 2014 p.9.</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Murray|first=Grahame|author2=Watt, Chris|title=Auschwitz survivor: 'Israel acts like Nazis'|publisher=[[Herald Scotland]]|date=24 January 2010|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/politics/auschwitz-survivor-israel-acts-like-nazis-1.1000918|accessdate=2 May 2010}}</ref> He went into hiding in 1943, but was arrested after a year and spent ten months in [[Auschwitz (concentration camp)|Auschwitz]]. After Auschwitz, he swore to never speak German again. He broke the rule at a scientific conference in Amsterdam after the war, when he happened to be speaking on a similar topic to that discussed by [[Hermann Haken]].<ref>Bernd Kröger, [https://books.google.com/books?id=h42aBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA39 ''Hermann Haken: From the Laser to Synergetics: A Scientific Biography of the Early Years,''] Springer, 2014 p.39 n.149.</ref>

His parents had originally been deported to [[Theresienstadt concentration camp]] in 1943, but after his father succumbed to an illness on 15 May 1944, it was decided by the Nazis that there was no more reason to allow his widow Therese to stay there, and that she should be deported to Auschwitz. However, she had hidden a cyanide capsule inside a piece of bread and chose suicide, knowing that the chances of survival there were non-existent.<ref>''Briefe,'' 2014 p.16.</ref> His correspondence with his parents while in exile during the war were published. The autobiography of his elder brother, Alfred, also dwells on their experiences during the war.<ref>Alfred G.Meyer, ''My Life as a Fish: A Memoir,'' Ann Arbor 2000 p,28.</ref>

==Post-Holocaust==
After the war, Meyer returned to the Netherlands, and studied [[theoretical physics]]. He eventually became director of the [[Philips Natuurkundig Laboratorium|Phillips Physics Laboratory]] (NatLab).<ref name=times2018 />

After his retirement he took courses in woodwork and constructed violins and violas.<ref name=times2018>Henry Zeffman, [https://www.thetimes.com/article/hajo-meyer-profile-physicist-who-survived-auschwitz-x76qtd0d5 'Hajo Meyer profile: Physicist who survived Auschwitz,'] [[The Times]] 1 August 2018.</ref> He built about 50 of them.<ref name=smolinski />

==Political career==
In his later years Meyer became politically active, becoming director of ''[[Een Ander Joods Geluid|A Different Jewish Voice]]''. He was a member of the [[International Jewish Anti-Zionist Network]],<ref>[https://www.ijan.org/uncategorized/honoring-hajo-meyer-on-holocaust-remembrance-day/ Honoring Hajo Meyer on Holocaust Remembrance Day], International Jewish Anti-Zionist Network, retrieved 18 June 2024</ref> founded in 2008 and the Dutch political party [[GroenLinks]].<ref>[https://joodsbw.nl/id/P-5019 Meyer, Hans-Joachim Gustav (Hajo) 1924 - 2014], Database Joods Biografisch Woordenboek, retrieved 18 June 2024</ref>

He was the first signatory of a statement by 250 Holocaust survivors and descendants of Holocaust survivors protesting the killings that were taking place during the [[2014 Israel-Gaza Conflict]].<ref>Suzanne Weiss, [https://www.greenleft.org.au/content/holocaust-survivor-condemns-gaza-massacre 'Holocaust survivor condemns Gaza massacre,'] [[Green Left Weekly]] Issue 1021 17 August 2014.</ref>

===Visit to Gaza and the West Bank===
In 2005 Meyer visited the [[Occupied Palestinian territories]], together with former Dutch prime minister [[Dries van Agt]] and other former ministers from Germany and Ireland, where he concluded that the [[Gaza Strip]] was "one big [[concentration camp]]". The situation in [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict in Hebron|Hebron]] he found even worse. [[Israeli settlers]] came to live in the middle of the city, which meant that thousands of Palestinian shops and businesses had to close. Palestinians who live in the city are being assaulted there on a regular basis. Meyer witnessed one assault that could easily have become deadly.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20061110115930/https://www.sp.nl/nieuws/tribune/200609/interview_hajo_meyer.shtml Interview - Hajo Meyer], Tribune, Nieuwsblad van de [[Socialistische Partij (Nederland)|SP]], 9 september 2006, retrieved 10 May 2025</ref>

===Book===
Meyer wrote a book titled ''Het einde van het Jodendom'' (''The End of Judaism'') in 2003,.{{efn|German edition ''Das Ende des Judentums. Der Verfall der israelischen Gesellschaft,''  Melzer Verlag, [[Neu Isenburg]] 2005}} In 2007 an English language edition of the book was published.<ref name=Meyer2007>Hajo G. Meyer - The End of Judaism: An Ethical Tradition Betrayed, 2007, {{ISBN|9781479180134}}</ref>

In his book, Meyer draws a comparison between the way Jews were treated in the 1930s by the Germans in Germany and later in The Netherlands, and what Israel is doing to the Palestinians, in Israel itself as well as in the occupied territories, all with the objective of making the Jews and Palestinians respectively, leave the country. It was not until this strategy began to fail that Hitler began to consider other solutions.<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.185</ref> Elements of this treatment were:
* Dehumanizing Jews by referring to them as animals, parasites, or a plague. The then Israeli Chief of Staff [[Moshe Ya'alon]] is quoted as speaking of the Palestinians as "cancer".<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.132</ref> Prime Minister [[Ariel Sharon]] later corroborated this statement as "true and correct".<ref name=Meyer224>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.224</ref> Former Minister of Education, [[Shulamit Aloni]], confirmed the demonization of the Arabs in Israeli schoolbooks.<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.169</ref>
* Exaggerating the threat. Hitler was obsessed by the notion that Jews were planning to sweep Germany from the map.<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.126</ref> Likewise Israelis insist that the Palestinians not only want to drive Israel into the sea, but actually have the capacity to do so.<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.128</ref>
* Intimidation and harassment by the armed forces. Meyer finds it particularly painful that his "own people" are now involved in similar behaviour towards the Palestinians.<ref name=134-135 />
* Inflicting economic hardship by banning Jews from certain professions and boycotting Jewish stores. Analogous economic pressure has been put on Palestinians.<ref name=134-135 />
* Not intervening when Jews were being harassed by non-Jewish citizens. Meyer recalls a [[Purim]] celebration for children that was broken up by the [[Sturmabteilung|SA]]. Complaints to the police had no effect. Israelis have been reported as [[Israeli settler violence|attacking]] Palestinian farmers during their harvesting and targeting Palestinian schools with impunity.<ref name=134-135>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.134-135</ref>
* Applying [[collective punishment]]. For instance: If a Jew did something that displeased the regime, his or her relatives could be punished for it. Likewise, if the IDF suspected a Palestinian to be a member of [[Hamas]], an entire apartment complex could be leveled.<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.128-129</ref>

The book accuses the successive governments of Israel of using the [[Holocaust]] to downplay the suffering and injustices they inflict on the [[Palestinians]].<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.179</ref>

"Contrary to what Israel's government would have everyone believe, criticism of Israel is not the same as anti-Semitism", Meyer writes.<ref name=187-191>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.187-191</ref> In fact: "...at present the only reason to expect a revival of dangerous anti-Semitism is Israel's increasingly reprehensible policies".<ref name=187-191 /> Meyer encourages non-Jews to "shed their guilt about the Holocaust" and feel free to criticize Jews who are clearly committing crimes.<ref name=187-191 /> He claims that Jewish people and organizations must openly distance themselves from the current Israeli policies.<ref name=187-191 />

Among other things, Meyer concludes that the State of Israel and Zionism have "failed" because they have not lived up to the promise of a safe haven for the persecuted Jews of the world.<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.218, p.221</ref>

In the [[Epigraph (literature)|epigraph]] of his book Meyer quotes [[Hillel the Elder|Rabbi Hillel]]: "That which is hateful to you do not do to your neighbor. That is the whole of the [[Torah]]." In the last chapter he states: "A people that has betrayed the basic ethical foundation of its long and astonishing survival will lack the vitality to preserve an identity of its own in the midst of an increasingly homogenous world".<ref>Hajo G. Meyer 2007, p.229</ref>

===Lectures===
During his lectures Meyer repeatedly argued that there are [[Comparisons between Israel and Nazi Germany|parallels between the Nazi treatment of Jews leading to (but not including) the Holocaust, and Israel's dehumanization of Palestinians]].<ref name="SmithBurr">David Whitten Smith, Elizabeth Geraldine Burr, [https://books.google.com/books?id=5v-iBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA101 ''Understanding World Religions: A Road Map for Justice and Peace,''] [[Rowman & Littlefield]] 2014 p.101-102.</ref> He expanded on this sense of an analogy in an article in the Huffington Post:

{{blockquote|I cannot help but hear echoes of the Nazi mythos of "blood and soil" in the rhetoric of settler fundamentalism which claims a sacred right to all the lands of biblical Judea and Samaria. The various forms of collective punishment visited upon the Palestinian people - coerced ghettoization behind a "security wall"; the bulldozing of homes and destruction of fields; the bombing of schools, mosques, and government buildings; an economic blockade that deprives people of the water, food, medicine, education and the basic necessities for dignified survival - force me to recall the deprivations and humiliations that I experienced in my youth.<ref name="Meyer2010">Hajo Meyer, [https://www.huffingtonpost.com/hajo-meyer/an-ethical-tradition-betr_b_438660.html 'An Ethical Tradition Betrayed,'] [[Huffington Post]] 25 May 2010</ref>}}

At one of his talks, organized and hosted by the leader of the UK's [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], [[Jeremy Corbyn]], in 2010, Meyer was later reported to have repeatedly likened Israel's actions against the people of the [[Gaza Strip]] to the mass killing of Jews in the Holocaust and the government of Israel to that of Nazi Germany.<ref name="Zeffman1">{{cite news |last1=Zeffman |first1=Henry |title=Jeremy Corbyn hosted event likening Israel to Nazis |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/jeremy-corbyn-hosted-event-likening-israel-to-nazis-6sb5rqd5x |access-date=1 August 2018 |work=The Times |date=1 August 2018 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Marsh1">Sarah Marsh, [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2018/aug/01/jeremy-corbyn-issues-apology-in-labour-antisemitism-row 'Corbyn apologises over event where Israel was compared to Nazis,'] [[The Guardian]] 1 August 2018</ref> During the talk, Meyer said that "Judaism in Israel has been substituted by the Holocaust religion, whose high priest is [[Elie Wiesel]]."<ref name="Zeffman1" />

Meyer participated in the 2011 "Never Again – For Anyone" tour. He argued there are different interpretations of Judaism, and that Jews ought to return to the principles of the [[Book of Leviticus]] and the rabbinical principles of figures like [[Hillel the Elder|Hillel]], and avoid the 'doomsday Judaism' he identifies in the [[Book of Joshua]] as well as the positions of [[Abraham Isaac Kook]] which have in his view underwritten Zionism.<ref>Moises F. Salinas, Hazza Abu Rabi, [https://books.google.com/books?id=zLPQk-QgABkC&pg=PA136 ''Resolving the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict: Perspectives on the Peace Process,''] Cambria Books, 2009 p.136</ref>

Meyer claimed that although Zionism predates [[fascism]], Zionists and fascists have had a history of cooperation, charging that, among other things, Israel desires to foment anti-Semitism in the world to encourage more Jews to migrate to Israel.<ref>M Ghazali Khan, {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20101225104659/http://www.indianmuslims.info/news/2006/july/02/articles/muslims_jews_and_christians_join_together_to_condemn_zionism.html 'Muslims, Jews and Christians Join Together to Condemn Zionism,']}} Indian Muslims org. 2 July 2006.</ref>

Meyer spoke in favor of the [[Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions]] movement against Israel.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kerrison|first=Mark|url=http://www.demotix.com/news/234627/auschwitz-survivor-supports-campaign-boycott-divestment-and-sanctions-against-israel|title=Auschwitz survivor supports campaign of boycott, divestment and sanctions against Israel|website=Demotix.com|date=29 January 2010|access-date=9 September 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923225900/http://www.demotix.com/news/234627/auschwitz-survivor-supports-campaign-boycott-divestment-and-sanctions-against-israel|archive-date=23 September 2015}}</ref>

==Accusation of antisemitism==
[[Henryk Broder]] publicly accused Meyer and his editor Abraham Melzer as being "capacities for applied [[Judeophobia]]" (''Kapazitäten für angewandte Judäophobie'') and producing "brown garbage" (''braunen Dreck''). Meyer and Melzer sued and in 2007 a court forbade Broder to make these statements.<ref>Hannes Stein, [https://www.welt.de/print-welt/article189802/Wer-ist-Antisemit-Henryk-M-Broder-und-Hajo-Meyer-vor-Gericht.html 'Wer ist Antisemit? Henryk M. Broder und Hajo Meyer vor Gericht,'] [[Die Welt]]  10 January.2006</ref><ref>[https://www.faz.net/aktuell/feuilleton/debatten/urteil-broder-darf-verleger-keine-judenfeindlichkeit-unterstellen-1302166.html 'Broder darf Verleger keine Judenfeindlichkeit unterstellen,'] [[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]] 27 January 2006.</ref> On appeal, a court mostly cleared Broder and Melzer saying that the statements were "legally admissible criticism" and stating that "[[Self-hating Jew|Jewish anti-Semitism]]" exists.<ref>Yves Pallade, [https://www.jstor.org/stable/25834824 ' "New" Anti-Semitism in contemporary German academia,'] [[Jewish Political Studies Review]], Vol. 21, No. 1/2 (Spring 2009), pp. 33-62 op.39</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/gesellschaft/medien/den-adolf-gemacht-6584329.html |title=Henryk M. Broder: "Den Adolf gemacht" |author=Alex Feuerherdt |work=[[Tagesspiegel]] |date=2007-11-09 |language=de |access-date=2025-04-29}}</ref>

==Death==
On 23 August 2014, Meyer died in his sleep in [[Heiloo]], Netherlands at the age of 90.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 August 2014 |title=Antizionist Hajo Meyer overleden |trans-title=Anti-Zionist Hajo Meyer passed away |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/690197-antizionist-hajo-meyer-overleden |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031171633/https://nos.nl/artikel/690197-antizionist-hajo-meyer-overleden.html |archive-date=31 October 2020 |access-date=28 January 2024 |website=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting|NOS]] |language=nl}}</ref>
